stem: Which feature set is most consistent with a typical febrile seizure?

options.text: Age 6 months to 6 years, generalised tonic-clonic seizure, brief duration, post-ictal phase
Afebrile seizure, focal features, prolonged duration, recurrent events
New neurological abnormality after the seizure

explanation: Typical febrile seizure features are age 6 months to 6 years, a generalised tonic-clonic seizure, brief duration, and a post-ictal phase.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Neurology Seizures - Emergency Management

optionExplanations.A: Correct because typical febrile seizures occur between 6 months and 6 years of age, are usually generalised tonic-clonic, brief, and followed by a post-ictal phase.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because afebrile, focal, prolonged, or recurrent seizures are not typical of a simple febrile seizure and suggest an alternative diagnosis.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because persistently altered neurology is a red flag and is not consistent with a typical febrile seizure.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because concern for meningitis points to a serious CNS infection rather than a typical febrile seizure.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because a new neurological abnormality after the event is a red flag and is not part of the typical febrile seizure pattern.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
